subject: Prototype: On-call Incident Snapshot for Route Anomaly Inspector
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, david.simmons@acme.com
Date: Sat, 04 Mar 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Prototype: On-call Incident Snapshot for Route Anomaly Inspector

Hi team —

Following up from last week's product/ops sync: Acme reported a support pain where the on-call engineer spends ~20–30 minutes collecting context for a high-cost spike (route X -> generates many tokens). They asked if we can ship a compact "Incident Snapshot" tile in Console that collects per-route cost delta, tail latency (95/99p), top error traces, a top-5 recent prompts sample (redacted), and a one-click link to create an Ops incident with relevant telemetry attached.

My ask: prototype a minimal incident snapshot tile we can show to Acme next week. Must-haves for the prototype:
- 15m/1h/24h cost deltas (USD) for the route
- 95th and 99th tail latency for the same window
- Flag if the route exceeded its configured token budget or SLO
- Small sample of recent prompts (redacted) and a link to copy to clipboard
- A link that opens a pre-filled incident (Jira or internal flow) with attached top traces

Non-blocking but high-value: heatmap view (route by percentile) and a one-click run of a diagnostic query that pulls the KV cache snapshot.

Questions I need answered before I commit this to OBS-412:
1) How expensive is the one-click diagnostic query to run on demand (ballpark cost / CPU)?
2) Can we include a small prompt sample without leaking PII? What's our redaction surface?
3) What retention window do we need for percentile tiering (do we aggregate daily/rollups)?

I've attached a mockup and a one-pager with the proposed UX. Meeting scheduled with Acme on Tue 9am PT — would like to share the prototype or a design walkthrough.

Attachments: mockup-incident-snapshot.png (PNG mockup)

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

---
Aditya Rao
Product / Console

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 05 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prototype: On-call Incident Snapshot for Route Anomaly Inspector

+1 on prototype — useful to have something concrete for Acme. A few quick product clarifications: 

- SLIs: we should be explicit about which SLI maps to the 95/99p latency. Is that server-side generation latency (inference) or end-to-end (including network + pre/post-processing)? For the prototype keep it inference-only to simplify.
- Alerting thresholds: do we expose the configured threshold on the tile (e.g., budget = $X/day) and show a yellow/red state? That helps on-call triage.
- Access controls: make sure the tile respects route-level visibility — not all org members should see the prompt samples.

On redaction: we should surface 1–3 prompts but run a light NLP scrub: remove sequences that look like emails, phone numbers, long UUIDs. If we cannot guarantee full PII removal in the pipeline, show 'sample unavailable' and a link to request a deeper audit (manual).

I'll attach a short SLA-proposal PDF with suggested SLI definitions and thresholds — this should help engineering pick defaults. If engineering can confirm the cost of on-demand diagnostics we can decide whether to run them automatically for critical incidents or keep them behind a button.

Lauren
Director, Observability Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-proposal.pdf (SLI/threshold suggestions)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Mar 2028 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prototype: On-call Incident Snapshot for Route Anomaly Inspector

Thanks for the clear ask, Aditya. Technical notes / constraints below: 

1) One-click diagnostic query cost: running an ad hoc percentile/trace aggregation across raw request logs is moderately expensive if we don't pre-aggregate. Ballpark: a 1-hour window across a busy tenant could consume ~10-30s of CPU on our telemetry nodes and incur ingestion/query units equivalent to one small dedicated job. To keep costs low we can:
   - Use pre-aggregated rollups (1m/5m) for cost/latency deltas (cheap)
   - Run full trace collection only when the user clicks the diagnostic button (on-demand) and cap it to top-N traces to bound cost

2) Prompt sample redaction: we already have a lightweight scrubber in the ingestion pipeline (removes obvious emails, phone numbers, common PII regex). However it doesn't catch proprietary secrets or long code extracts. Proposal: show the sample with a prominent "Redaction applied" badge and a link to request a secure review. For Acme demo we'll toggle it off only in a private meeting with their security rep present.

3) Retention and rollups: For percentiles we keep per-route histograms for 90 days at 1m rollups and 365 days as daily aggregates. That should be enough for the prototype. If product wants finer-grained long-term queries, we'll need to add an LTT (long-term telemetry) job.

Implementation plan for prototype (2 sprint plan):
- Sprint 1: UI tile + read-only rollup calls for cost and percentiles (use existing metrics endpoints).
- Sprint 2: Add prompt-sample widget (with redaction), diagnostic one-click that triggers a background trace collector, and incident prefill link (Jira integration).

We can reuse Grafana panels for the heatmap if product wants quicker turnaround — otherwise we build a native Console tile.

Attaching a quick runbook for canarying the diagnostic path and an updated cost estimate.

Jasmine
Senior Software Engineer, Observability
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 07 Mar 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prototype: On-call Incident Snapshot for Route Anomaly Inspector

This looks good — I approve moving OBS-412 into sprint 46 as a prototype. Action items / constraints from infra/ops: 

- Jasmine: please implement the Sprint 1 read-only rollup calls first. Limit the initial diagnostic to the top-10 traces and cap runtime to 60s; ensure background job uses priority queue so it does not impact live serving.
- Lauren / Aditya: confirm the exact SLI name and default thresholds (Lauren, can you add these to the Jira ticket?).
- Security: we will default to showing "Redaction applied" and a link to request a secure dump. No raw prompt text will be surfaced by default.
- Canary: schedule a canary run against a non-critical Dedicated pool (I've attached a short checklist). We'll do a 48h canary before showing to Acme.

I'll join the Tue 9am PT meeting. If we hit blocking costs on the diagnostic, we can fallback to a lighter heatmap-only demo.

Vivek
Head of Reliability & Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary-checklist.md
